explanations.explanation: Music it is, friend. David, Israel's king, put these Levites in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark rested there (1 Chronicles 6:31). Think of it as the most important job in the whole bakery: nobody gets through a long batch without a little song. Mine is mostly humming and a timer that doesn't care.

The treasury is a fair guess, since somebody always has to watch the money. But the text says David put these men in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark rested there (1 Chronicles 6:31). Nothing about counting coins. I'd be a terrible treasurer anyway, because my whole bank account used to be a 25 cent price sticker.

Gates are a real job, but they aren't the one in this verse. The text says David put these men in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark rested there (1 Chronicles 6:31). So these Levites weren't standing at a door. They were making a joyful noise, and nobody had to check a ticket.

Tabernacle, yes! The singers ministered with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon, David's son, built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6:32). So the music started in a tent. Big things can start small, and I know that from a bin at a closing bakery.

I see why you'd pick the palace, since David was king. But the text says they ministered with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting (1 Chronicles 6:32). This music was for the LORD's house, not for the king's living room. Nobody was performing for a throne.

A gate would make a fine stage, friend, but that's not what the verse says. The singers ministered with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6:32). Their spot was the tent itself. Standing in a doorway singing would just block traffic.

explanations.answer: According to the regulations given them
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The singers performed their duties "according to the regulations given them." (1 Chronicles 6:32) So even the music had an order to it. I can respect that, because even my cookies come out better when I follow the recipe instead of my feelings.

That sounds like a loose kitchen where everybody does their own thing, and I've seen how that ends. But the text says they performed their duties "according to the regulations given them." (1 Chronicles 6:32) So there were set regulations, not whatever each leader felt like that morning. Free-style baking is for dough, not for this.

explanations.answer: Only when the king was there
explanations.explanation: Good thinking, since David was the one who put them in charge (1 Chronicles 6:31). But the verse never says they waited on the king. It says they performed their duties "according to the regulations given them." (1 Chronicles 6:32) Their schedule came from those regulations, not from who was in the room.

explanations.answer: Every kind of service of the tabernacle
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, friend. Their fellow Levites "were assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God." (1 Chronicles 6:48) Every kind! That's a long list, and I bet somebody was always wiping something down. I know that life, because I once had to scrub my own apron.

explanations.answer: Guarding the gates of the king's palace
explanations.explanation: That's a creative job description, but it's not in this verse. The text says the other Levites were assigned to "every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God." (1 Chronicles 6:48) Their work was at the tabernacle, not at a palace. No fancy front door to stand at.

explanations.answer: Collecting the taxes from every tribe
explanations.explanation: Nobody enjoys a tax collector showing up, so I get the guess. But the text says the other Levites were assigned to "every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God." (1 Chronicles 6:48) Their work was serving at the tabernacle. Not one word about collecting money.

I get the thought, because the Levites were all busy at the tabernacle. But the text says Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place (1 Chronicles 6:49). The other Levites were assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle (1 Chronicles 6:48). So the Most Holy Place was Aaron and his sons' job, and no one else shared it.

False is right, baker. The text says "Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place." (1 Chronicles 6:49) The other Levites had plenty to do, since they were assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle (1 Chronicles 6:48), but that room's work wasn't theirs. Some jobs have one set of hands, like my cookie stamp.

That's it, friend. Aaron and his sons presented the offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense "to make atonement for Israel." (1 Chronicles 6:49) That's the heart of their work, and it's serious business. It points me toward Jesus, the Lamb, who gave His life to rescue people (Mark 10:45).

The towns come up later in the chapter, so I see how you got there. But the verse says the offerings were presented "to make atonement for Israel." (1 Chronicles 6:49) The altars were about atonement, not about dedicating towns. The city list is a separate part of the chapter.

explanations.answer: To ask for rain on the land
explanations.explanation: Rain is a big deal for any land, no argument from me. But the text says Aaron and his sons presented the offerings "to make atonement for Israel." (1 Chronicles 6:49) That's the stated purpose, and rain isn't mentioned here at all.

True, baker! Aaron and his sons did their work "according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded." (1 Chronicles 6:49) Moses, Israel's leader, gave the instructions, and they followed them. That's the kind of baking I like, where you read the whole recipe first, which I rarely do.

I can see being careful here, but the text says it plainly. Aaron and his sons did their work "according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded." (1 Chronicles 6:49) So it's true, and they followed what Moses, Israel's leader, had commanded. No freelancing in the Most Holy Place.

explanations.answer: The first lot fell to them
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend! The text says they come first "because the first lot fell to them." (1 Chronicles 6:54) So it came down to the lot, and nobody had to argue over who goes first. I wish my cookie sheet worked like that.

David was a big part of this chapter, so I get it. But the text gives the reason: "because the first lot fell to them." (1 Chronicles 6:54) It was the lot that put them first. David's name isn't attached to this part.

Biggest first makes sense in a lot of lines, like the line at a cookie sale. But this verse doesn't say a word about size. It says "because the first lot fell to them." (1 Chronicles 6:54) The lot decided it.
